assessment: The incumbent supplies a recurring conversational routine, printed access, and optional messaging. Seven frequent attendees found the repeated structure helpful, supporting retention of that scaffold. The concrete limit is five occasional attendees struggling to enter conversations familiar to their partners; continuity may benefit some while hindering entry for others, but causation is unproved. Of 72 slips, 49 reported the speaking target and 48 named the intended preparation task. These do not establish success across 97 attendances; missing slips, untimed speech, and unlinked weeks limit inference. Coordination sometimes exceeded 90 minutes. Pair delays and partner changes identify friction without establishing its cause.

openings.claim: A self-contained opening prompt with alternating short speaking turns may help occasional attendees enter conversation while retaining the familiar session structure.
openings.delta: Make entry independent of shared prior-session context without requiring public proficiency labels or prior attendance.
openings.prediction: Compared with ordinary prompts, occasional attendees will start substantive speech sooner and report easier entry; frequent attendees will retain useful practice. If only formation delays matter, post-pairing entry measures should change little.
openings.probe: Within existing sessions, randomly offer pairs either the ordinary opening or a self-contained opening with alternating turns. Anonymously observe time from seating to each partner's first substantive contribution and speaking distribution; collect usefulness and optional attendance-frequency reports. Record added volunteer minutes.
assumptions: Opening prompts fit existing printing and session time.
Observed sessions are not sufficient alone to establish six-session success.

openings.claim: A visibly dated, single next-task box on every printed sheet may reduce confusion between current and earlier preparation instructions.
openings.delta: Distinguish instruction-version confusion from failure to obtain instructions.
openings.prediction: Among recipients, earlier-task answers should decrease; errors concentrated among nonrecipients would instead indicate an access problem.
openings.probe: Introduce the box using existing printing. On anonymous exit slips ask which dated sheet was received and the next task; compare error categories with baseline and log preparation-related coordination minutes.
assumptions: The intended next task is settled before printing.
Dating alone does not provide absent learners with advance access.
Before-after changes cannot establish causation alone.
